title: SEO decisioning
when_to_use: Do I need an SEO plugin, recommend SEO, install Yoast/Rank Math/AIOSEO, search visibility.
principles: One SEO plugin is enough — never install a second while another major SEO plugin is active.
Check blog_public first: if search engines are discouraged, fixing visibility matters before plugin setup.
“Do I need an SEO plugin?” → inspect stack; many sites already have Yoast, Rank Math, AIOSEO, The SEO Framework, Squirrly, etc.
Recommend for THIS site (existing plugins, Woo, multilingual) — not a fixed brand favorite every time.
Install + activate with HITL when the user wants one set up; configure deep settings only when abilities exist.
steps: get-option blog_public; warn if discourage-search-engines is on for a site they want indexed.
list-plugins: identify active SEO / sitemap / redirect plugins.
If a capable SEO plugin is active → explain they likely do not need another; offer page-level help or settings links.
If inactive SEO plugin is installed → prefer activate over installing a competitor.
If none: search-plugins (e.g. "SEO"), pick one fit, install → activate (HITL chain).
After activate: point to the plugin’s settings via admin links; do not claim rankings will jump overnight.
anti_patterns: Installing Yoast when Rank Math (or another SEO plugin) is already active.
Ignoring blog_public=0 while obsessing over meta titles.
Promising traffic or ranking outcomes without data.
